title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This incident shows a generative image model being used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real, identifiable person. The failure occurred at the content creation stage, before any distribution, when photographs from a private social media account were turned into explicit synthetic images without the person's consent. The model did not assert a false fact; it produced realistic images that were then used to harass.

Catching this would have required either the image generation tool to refuse requests involving real people's photos without verified consent, or the social platforms where the images circulated to detect and remove non-consensual synthetic media. The use of multiple fake accounts and email addresses shows that identity checks on distribution platforms were also bypassed.

What is not established is any conviction or legal finding; the arrest and police account are allegations, and the investigation is ongoing.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media accounts and used AI technology to create morphed explicit content. He then shared this material through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The case began when the 22-year-old victim reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving anonymous messages informing her that her manipulated images and videos were circulating on Discord servers. Police conducted a detailed investigation analyzing digital footprints and technical evidence from the fake profiles, which revealed connections between multiple accounts linked to Bansal. During interrogation, Bansal revealed he knew the woman from college and harbored personal resentment toward her. Investigators recovered his mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence. The investigation is ongoing.
